questions.question: All the __________ countries likely to have Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__democratic__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A democratic country has a system of government in which the people have the power to participate in decision-making.
 
• A constitution is an aggregate of fundamental principles or established precedents that constitutethe legal basis of polity, organisation or other type of entity and commonly determine how that entity is to be governed. 
 
• All democratic countries are most likely to have a constitution.
 
• However, there are exceptions as a democratic country may not have a constitution.
 
• For example, Britain does not have a codified constitution.
 
• All countries that have a constitution are not necessarily democractic.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oligarchic **- A government or system in which power is held by a select few individuals or a small class of powerful people.
 
• **Communist - **It is a** **political and economic doctrine that aims to replace private property and a profit-based economy with public ownership and communal control of at least the major means of production (e.g., mines, mills, and factories) and the natural resources of a society.
 
• **Totalitarian **- a country or a system of government in which there is only one political party that has absolute power and control over the people.

questions.question: Dekhni is a folk dance associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Goa.__​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dekhni dance represents an attractive mixture of folk culture and Western music, danced mostly by Christian girls in fully Indian dress.
 
• The gestures in the dance appear to have been borrowed from the Kathak and Bharata Natyam.
 
• Dekhni in Konkani language means bewitching beauty.
 
• Dekhni dance is one of the oldest dance forms of Goa.
 
• Dekhni dance can be associated with those people who converted into Christianity from Hinduism during Portuguese rule.
 
• Dekhni Dance is performed by a group of girls caring earthen oil lamps in their hands.
 
• These girls are represented as the servants of God in this dance form. It represents the life of a devadasi.
 
• Ghumat Drum is the main instrument used in this dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hanv Saiba Poltodi Vetam is one of the most famous songs of Dekni dance.
 
• It was written by Carlos Eugenio Ferreira.
 
• This song was first published in 1895 in Paris and then in Goa in 1926.
 
• This song talks about a dancer who wanted to cross the river but the boatman refused to take her because the river was very rough that day.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the Open Market Operations by the Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market
Buying and selling of bonds issued by commercial banks in the open market
Only buying of bonds issued by the Government in the open market
Only selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Open Market Operations (OMO) is conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the sale or purchase of government securities (g-secs), financial assets or bonds issued by the government to the banks in order to adjust the money supply.

 
 
• The RBI does this to regulate the liquidity from the system and to infuse liquidity into the system.
 
 
 
• There are two types of Open Market Operations: Outright Purchase and Repurchase Agreement. Hence option 1 is correct.
 
 
• Outright Purchase or PEMO is a permanent transaction which involves the RBI selling or purchasing securities in the open market to regulate the money supply.
 
• A Repurchase Agreement is a short-term agreement that involves the RBI buying and purchasing government securities after a specified date.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Open Market Operations are flexible and easily reversible thereby reducing the lags of monetary policy.
 
• In 1948, the RBI mentioned the OMO purchase for the first time in its Annual Report.
 
• Government securities or G-Secs are tradable instruments issued by central governments and state governments.
 
• They are risk-free instruments and can be short-term like Treasury bills (T-bills) with a maturity of less than a year or long-term like government bonds with a maturity of a year or more than a year.

questions.question: In 1931, who recognised that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, which can mathematically be written as 4n + 2 (n = 0, 1, 2, 3 etc.)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Erich Huckel__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Erich Huckel was a German chemist and physicist.
 
• He proposed a theory in 1931 to help determine if a planar ring molecule would have aromatic properties.
 
• Erich Huckel recognized that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons.
 
• His rule states that a cyclic, planar molecule is considered aromatic if it has 4n+2 pi electrons.
 
• This rule is known as Huckel's Rule.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pi bond:- Bond formed by the same phase overlap of atomic orbitals along a direction perpendicular to the internuclear axis is called pi bond.
 
• Pi electrons:- An electron that resides in the pi bond (s) of a double bond or a triple bond or in a conjugated p orbital is called pi electron.
 
• ​System is divided into aromatic, anti-aromatic, and non-aromatic based on no. of pi electrons-
 
 
• ​​​Aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an aromatic system is determined by N = 4n+2 (n is an integer)
 
• Anti-aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an anti-aromatic system is determined by N = 4n (n is an integer)
 
• Non-aromatic - If a compound does not have a continuous ring of conjugated p orbitals in a planar module, then it is called non-aromatic.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct with respect to the Prashastis and land grants?

I. Prashastis were composed by learned Brahmanas.

II. Kings often rewarded Brahmanas by grants of land which were recorded on copper plates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Prashastis.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Prashastis is a special kind of inscription, meaning “in praise of”. 
 
• They were composed by learned Brahmans in praise of the rulers. (***statement 1 is correct)***
 
• They tell us how rulers of that time wanted to illustrate themselves.
 
• If the kings liked the prashastis, they gave land as a gift to the Brahmans, with records of it on copper plates. (***statement 2 is correct)***
 
• The prashastis generally contained ornate titles, links to mythical legends or comparisons to deities, and often fabricated stories about wars, victories, loot, and attributes.
 
• The earliest well-known example of an extensive prashasti is the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela inscribed in or about the 1st century BCE in the Prakrit language and Brahmi script.
 
• The earliest prashastic inscription in the classical Sanskrit language is the Junagadh rock inscription of Rudradaman (circa 150 CE), which became a prototype for Gupta-era poetic prashastis in Sanskrit. 

Examples of Prashasti__

 
• Nashik prashasti (2nd century CE), of the Satavahana dynasty.
 
• Prayaga prashasti (4th century CE), Gupta Empire: Lists the rulers against whom the Gupta king Samudragupta fought.
 
• It also describes the policy that he followed toward each set of rulers.
 
• Velvikudi inscription (c. 8th century CE), of Pandya dynasty.
 
• Deopara Prashasti (12th century CE), of the Sena dynasty.

questions.question: In Tennis, what is the score when the receiver wins the next point after deuce?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advantage out**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tennis is a game played on a rectangular-shaped court, which can be one of many surfaces.
 
• It is either played with two players (singles match), or four players (doubles match).
 
• Players stand on opposite sides of the net and use a stringed racquet to hit the ball back and forth to each other.
 
• Most tennis matches are played in a best-of-three format, which means that players need to win 2 sets to win the match.
 
• The score when the receiver wins the next point after deuce **Advantage out**.
 
• In Grand Slams, men play best-of-five sets while women play best-of-three sets.
 
• Doubles matches are best-of-3 with a 10-point tiebreak in lieu of the third set.
 
• USTA and club matches are usually best-of-3.
 
• There are two main ways of scoring a set.
 
 
• Advantage Set
 
 
• In an advantage set, a player or team needs to win six games, by two, to win the set.
 
• This means that there is no tiebreak game played at 6-6.
 
• The set continues until one player/team wins by two games.
 
 
 
• Tiebreak Set
 
 
• In a tiebreak set, a player or team needs to win six games wins a set.
 
• If the score gets to 5-5 (5-all), one player must win the next two games to win the set.
 
• If the score reaches 6-6 (6-all) in the set, a tiebreak game is played.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tennis is an Olympic sport and is played at all levels of society and at all ages.

questions.question: What is the correct statement related to Avogadro?

options.text: Avogadro made a distinction between electrons and neutrons.
Avogadro discovered a difference between animal and plant cell.
Avogadro made a distinction between atoms and molecules.

questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Avogadro made a distinction between atoms and molecules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Avogadro is a term that refers to two related concepts in chemistry:

**Avogadro's number:**

 
• This is a **fundamental constant** in **chemistry** that represents the **number of atoms or molecules** in **one mole of a substance. *(Option 4 is correct)***
 
• Its value is approximately **6.022 x 10^²³**, and it is denoted by the symbol "N_A".
 
• **Avogadro's number** is a key concept in **stoichiometry.** 
 
• The branch of chemistry deals with the **quantitative relationships **between **reactants and products** in **chemical reactions.**

**Amedeo Avogadro:**

 
• He is **best known** for his **contributions** to the **development of the mole concept in chemistry**.
 
• **Avogadro** proposed that **equal volumes of gases** at the **same temperature** and **pressure** contain the **same number of particles**, which led to the development of **Avogadro's law.**
 
• He also proposed the **hypothesis** that the **same volume of different gases,** **at the same temperature** and** pressure**, contains an** equal number of molecules**. This hypothesis became known as **Avogadro's principle.**
 
• **Avogadro's contributions** to the development of the **mole concept** and the **understanding of the behavior of gases** have had a profound impact on the field of chemistry.

questions.question: ‘Anaconda’ one of the world’s largest snakes is found in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical evergreen forest.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Tropical evergreen forests:

__
 
• Tropical evergreen forests have trees that always have leaves and have a shade look.
 
• They always receive heavy rainfall i.e greater than 200 cm.
 
• The temperature that is maintained is between 20-27o C.
 
• The trees reach great heights up to 60 metres or even above.
 
• These are generally found in the Western Ghats, Andaman, and Nicobar, North East Area.
 
• Examples of tropical evergreen are Rubber, Beetle Nut, Jamun, Mango, Roseberry, and Bamboo.
 
• These forests have a multilayered structure with trees, shrubs and creepers.
 
• There is no definite time for trees to shed their leaves.
 
• As such, these forests appear green all year round.
 
• Anacondas can be seen in the Amazon River.
 
 
• Anacondas are a group of large snakes found in the tropical evergreen forest of South America.
 
• Only four species of Anacondas are currently recognized.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​Semi-evergreen forests:

__
 
• Semi-evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Eastern Himalayas.
 
• Such forests have a mixture of wet evergreen trees and moist deciduous trees.
 
• The forest is dense and is filled with a large variety of trees of both types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfe2d3a87648c708fd83649ca3d8d71312987c45d5687748675e5d8382b35a42.png]

questions.question: Battle of Buxar was fought in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1764__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought between the English Forces (Hector Munro – British Army Major), and a joint army of the Nawab of Oudh, Nawab of Bengal, and the Mughal Emperor.
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764. Hence the correct answer is 1764. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The reasons for battle were:

 
• Mir Qasim wanted to be independent and shifted his capital to Munger Fort from Calcutta. 
 
• These factors fuelled the English to overthrow him and war broke out between Mir Kasim and the Company in 1763.
 
• Participants of the Battle of Buxar were:
 
 
• Mir Qasim – (Administering Bengal in place of Mir Jafar – Nawab of Bengal)
 
• Shuja-Ud-Daulah – Nawab of Awadh (Oudh)
 
• Shah Alam II – Mughal Emperor
 
 

Result of Battle of Buxar:

 
• Mir Jafar (Nawab of Bengal) handed over districts of Midnapore, Burdwan, and Chittagong to the English for the maintenance of their army.
 
• The English were also permitted duty-free trade in Bengal, except for a duty of two per cent on salt.
 
• Clive made political settlements with Emperor Shah Alam II and Shuja-Ud-Daula of Awadh in the Treaty of Allahabad.

questions.question: In June 2022, AGNIPATH scheme was launched by the central government for which of the following purposes?

options.text: Recruitment of youth in the Armed Forces
Popularising the use of non-plastic alternatives
Sustainable and inclusive development of metro cities
Providing house facilities to tea garden workers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Recruitment of youth in the Armed Forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Centre has cleared the AGNIPATH Scheme for recruitment of youth in the armed forces.
 
• The youth selected under this scheme will be known as Agniveers.
 
• They will be getting an attractive monthly package with risk and hardship allowances as applicable in the three services.
 
• They will be also paid a one-time Seva Nidhi Package upon completion of the engagement period of four years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• ​‘Agniveers’will form a distinct rank in the three services, and will also wear a distinct insignia as part of their uniform.
 
• The ‘Agnipath’ model envisages the recruitment of personnel below officer rank (PBOR) in the army, air force and navy for four years, including six months of training.
 
• The soldiers recruited under ‘Agnipath’ will be released from service after four years, though the new system will have a provision for retaining around 25% of them after another round of screening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhopal Gas Tragedy:

 
 
• It was a gas leak incident that happened in India on 3rd December 1984.
 
• The leakage of toxic methyl isocyanate gas at a Union Carbide plant was the cause of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.
 
• Union Carbide plant was owned by the Indian subsidiary of the American firm Union Carbide Corporation.
 
• About 45 tons of the dangerous gas methyl isocyanate leaked from an insecticide plant.
 
• Methyl isocyanate is an extremely toxic gas and its concentration in the air touches 21ppm (parts per million).
 
 
• It can cause death within minutes of inhaling the gas.
 
 
 
• The final death toll was estimated to be between 15,000 and 20,000.
 
• Some half a million survivors suffered respiratory problems, eye irritation or blindness, and other maladies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Bhopal:

 
• Due to various natural and artificial lakes, it is known as the City of Lakes.
 
• It is also one of the greenest cities in India.
 
• It is the 16th largest city in India and 131st in the world.
 
• Bhojtaal is also known as Bada Talab is the oldest man-made lake in India.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was received by Vempati Chinna Satyam, an Indian Kuchipudi dancer, in 1998?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Bhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vempati Chinna Satyam, who lived from 15 October 1929 to 29 July 2012, was a legend in the Kuchipudi dancing style.
 
• He is credited with spreading the dancing style's popularity all over the world.
 
• He has received numerous honours, including the Raja Lakshmi Award from Madras and the Sangeet Peeth of Bombay.
 
• He received** **Padma Bhushan award in 1998.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak Dance

 
 
• One of the primary categories of ancient Indian classical dance, known as Kathak, is thought to have started with the wandering storytellers known as Kathakars in North India.
 
• Similar to the early Greek theatre, these wandering Kathakars used music, dance, and songs to convey legendary tales.
 
• The Bhakti movement, a tendency of theistic devotion that emerged in mediaeval Hinduism, is when the genre first came into being.
 
 
 
• Manipuri Dance
 
 
• Manipuri dance is one of India's most well-known classical dance genres and is particularly renowned for its Vaishnavist themes and spectacular performances of dance dramas centred on the love between Radha and Krishna known as "Ras Lila."
 
• Additional subjects in this kind of art related to Shaktism, Shaivism, and the sylvan gods known as Umang Lai during the Manipuri festival "Lai Haraoba."
 
• Although this dance style has its roots in the ancient Sanskrit Hindu literature "Natya Shastra," it is named after the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur, where it first appeared.
 
 
 
• Kathakali Dance
 
 
• An essential subgenre of Indian classical dance known as "Kathakali" is linked to this kind of storytelling.
 
• It is a dance drama from Kerala in southern India. Like other Indian traditional dance forms, "Kathakali" uses spectacular facial and hand movements along with music and vocal performance to effectively convey the story to the audience.

questions.question: Which dynasty bronze statues were made using the “lost wax” technique?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The lost-wax technique (Cire Perdue):

__
 
• Used for making the bronze statues.
 
• In this technique, wax figures are first coated with wet clay and allowed to dry.
 
• The clay coated figures are then heated, allowing the wax inside to melt.
 
• The wax is then poured out through a tiny hole and liquid metal is poured inside the hollow mould.
 
• After the metal has cooled down and solidified, the clay coat is removed and a metal figure of the same shape as the wax figure is obtained.
 
• Chola Dynasty also used this technique to make bronze statues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Example: The Dancing Girl

 
 
• It is the world’s oldest bronze sculpture.
 
• Found in Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It is a 4-inch figure that depicts a naked girl wearing only ornaments, which include bangles in the left arm, and an amulet and bracelet on the right arm.
 
• She stands in a ‘Tribhanga’ dancing posture with the right hand on her hip.

questions.question: The Supreme Court on 18 July, 2022 ordered its registry to work out a mechanism to remove personal details of persons entangled in matrimonial litigation. This decision was taken to recognize which right as part of ‘right to privacy’?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Right to be forgotten**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Supreme Court's** decision to remove the personal details of individuals involved in **matrimonial litigation is a recognition of the right to privacy.**
 
• This **right is a fundamental right** that is protected under **Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The **court's decision** is in line with the **landmark judgment in the Puttaswamy case (2017)**.
 
• **Supreme Court** declared that the **right to privacy** is a **fundamental right** that is essential to the **dignity** and **autonomy of individuals.**
 
• The **court recognized** that the **right to privacy** includes the **right to control** the **dissemination of personal information.** 
 
• This decision is a step towards protecting that right for individuals involved in **matrimonial disputes.**
